question: Under Minnesota's foreclosure by advertisement statute, which of the following is a required precondition before a mortgage may be foreclosed by advertisement?
choice_a: The lender must first obtain a court judgment confirming the amount of the default
choice_b: The borrower must consent in writing to the foreclosure sale date
choice_c: A default in a condition of the mortgage has occurred that makes the power of sale operative, and no separate action to recover the debt is pending (or any such action has been discontinued or returned unsatisfied)
choice_d: A licensed appraiser must certify the current fair market value of the property
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 580.02 lists the requisites for foreclosure by advertisement, including that a default making the power of sale operative has occurred and that no action at law is pending to recover the debt secured by the mortgage (or any such action has been discontinued, or execution on a judgment in it returned unsatisfied), along with proper recording of the mortgage and any assignments.

question: In a standard Minnesota mortgage foreclosure by advertisement, what is the default statutory redemption period for the mortgagor after the foreclosure sale?
choice_a: 30 days from the date of the foreclosure sale
choice_b: Two years from the date of the foreclosure sale
choice_c: There is no post-sale redemption right in Minnesota
choice_d: Six months from the date of the foreclosure sale
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 580.23 provides that a mortgagor may redeem the foreclosed property within six months after the foreclosure sale by paying the sale price plus interest and allowable costs, unless one of the statutory conditions extending the period to 12 months applies.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 580.23, the standard six-month redemption period is extended to twelve months when the mortgaged property, at the time the mortgage was executed, exceeded what size?
choice_a: Ten acres
choice_b: One acre
choice_c: 40 acres
choice_d: 80 acres
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 580.23 extends the redemption period to twelve months if the mortgaged land exceeded ten acres in size at the time the mortgage was executed, along with other extending conditions such as mortgages executed before July 1, 1967, or the amount due being less than two-thirds of the original principal.

question: If a certificate of sale from a Minnesota mortgage foreclosure does not state an interest rate, what rate of interest accrues on the redemption amount by default under Minn. Stat. § 580.23?
choice_a: Ten percent per annum
choice_b: Six percent per annum
choice_c: Four percent per annum
choice_d: No interest accrues if the certificate is silent
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 580.23 states that redemption interest accrues at the rate specified in the certificate of sale, or, if no rate is stated, at six percent per annum.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 582.032, a court may reduce the post-sale mortgage redemption period on certain abandoned property to how short a period?
choice_a: One week from the date of sale
choice_b: Three months from the date of sale
choice_c: Five weeks from the date the reduction order is entered
choice_d: The redemption period cannot be reduced under any circumstances
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 582.032 allows a court, upon a finding of abandonment, to reduce the redemption period to five weeks (from the order if entered after the sale), applicable to property of ten acres or less improved with a residential dwelling of fewer than five units that is not a model home, dwelling under construction, or agricultural property.

question: Which of the following properties could qualify for the reduced five-week redemption period for abandoned property under Minn. Stat. § 582.032?
choice_a: A 200-acre actively farmed parcel with a farmhouse
choice_b: A model home currently being used by a builder for showings
choice_c: A 20-unit occupied apartment building
choice_d: A vacant, boarded-up single-family home on a two-acre lot with utilities disconnected and evidence of trespass
explanation: The reduced five-week redemption period under § 582.032 applies only to abandoned property of ten acres or less improved with a residential dwelling of fewer than five units, excluding model homes, dwellings under construction, and agricultural-use property; boarded windows, disconnected utilities, and evidence of trespass are listed as prima facie evidence of abandonment.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 580.03, how long must the notice of a Minnesota mortgage foreclosure by advertisement be published before the sale?
choice_a: Six weeks
choice_b: Two weeks
choice_c: Ten days
choice_d: Six months
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 580.03 requires six weeks' published notice that the mortgage will be foreclosed by sale of the mortgaged premises.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 580.03, if the mortgaged premises are actually occupied, by when must the notice of foreclosure sale be served on the person in possession?
choice_a: At least one year before the date of sale
choice_b: At least four weeks before the date of sale
choice_c: On the same day as the sale
choice_d: There is no separate service requirement on an occupant
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 580.03 requires that, when the mortgaged premises are actually occupied, notice must be served on the person in possession at least four weeks before the sale, using the same method used to serve a civil summons.

question: For a Minnesota contract for deed executed after August 1, 1985, what is the standard statutory notice period a seller must give a defaulting purchaser before canceling the contract under Minn. Stat. § 559.21?
choice_a: 10 days
choice_b: One year
choice_c: 60 days
choice_d: There is no notice requirement if the purchaser is more than 30 days late
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 559.21 sets a standard 60-day notice of cancellation period for contracts for deed executed after August 1, 1985, with shorter or longer periods applying in specific circumstances (such as certain earnest money or investor-seller contracts).

question: Which statement correctly describes a purchaser's rights during the statutory notice period after a seller serves a notice of cancellation of a Minnesota contract for deed under Minn. Stat. § 559.21?
choice_a: The purchaser has no right to cure and must vacate the property immediately upon service of the notice
choice_b: The purchaser may only reinstate the contract by paying off the full remaining balance
choice_c: The purchaser automatically receives fee title to the property once the notice is served
choice_d: The purchaser may reinstate the contract by curing the default and making the required payments within the notice period, or seek a court order suspending the termination pending resolution of claims or defenses
explanation: Under Minn. Stat. § 559.21, a purchaser served with a notice of cancellation may reinstate the contract during the notice period by curing the default, paying past-due amounts, service costs, and any statutory reinstatement charge, or may instead obtain a court order suspending the termination until claims or defenses are finally resolved.

question: Minn. Stat. § 559.21 requires the statutory notice of cancellation for a Minnesota contract for deed to be printed in what format?
choice_a: 12-point or larger, underlined, uppercase type stating that proceedings have begun under section 559.21 to terminate the contract
choice_b: Any font size, as long as it is on letterhead
choice_c: Handwritten and notarized only
choice_d: Braille format is legally required in all cases
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 559.21 mandates that specific statutory language, including notice that cancellation proceedings have begun under section 559.21, appear in 12-point or larger underlined uppercase type in the notice of cancellation.

question: In a Minnesota judicial foreclosure (foreclosure by action) under Chapter 581, when does the redemption period referenced in Minn. Stat. §§ 580.23 and 582.032 begin to run?
choice_a: From the date the complaint was filed
choice_b: From the date of the order of confirmation of the sale
choice_c: From the date the mortgage was originally recorded
choice_d: Redemption is not available after a judicial foreclosure sale
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 581.10 provides that after a foreclosure by action, the mortgagor (or those claiming under the mortgagor) may redeem within the time specified in section 580.23 or 582.032, measured from the date of the order confirming the sale.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 510.02, what is the maximum acreage a homestead may include in Minnesota, regardless of whether the property is urban or rural?
choice_a: 40 acres
choice_b: 10 acres
choice_c: 160 acres
choice_d: There is no acreage limit on a homestead
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 510.02 states that a homestead may include any quantity of land not exceeding 160 acres.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 510.02, Minnesota provides two dollar-value tiers for the homestead exemption from creditors' claims. Which pairing is correct?
choice_a: The agricultural and general homestead exemption amounts are always identical
choice_b: Only agricultural homesteads receive any dollar exemption at all
choice_c: The exemption amount is fixed permanently and is never adjusted
choice_d: A higher exemption amount applies to homesteads used primarily for agricultural purposes than applies to a general (non-agricultural) homestead
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 510.02 sets a higher dollar exemption for homesteads used primarily for agricultural purposes than for a general homestead, and both amounts are periodically adjusted for inflation under the mechanism referenced in section 550.37, subdivision 4a.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 510.01, Minnesota's homestead exemption from seizure or sale for debts does NOT protect the homestead against which type of claim?
choice_a: A debt incurred for work or materials furnished in the construction, repair, or improvement of the homestead itself
choice_b: A general unsecured credit card debt owed by the homeowner
choice_c: A personal injury judgment unrelated to the property
choice_d: A debt owed to a friend for an unrelated personal loan
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 510.01 exempts the homestead from seizure or sale for most debts, but expressly carves out debts incurred for work or materials furnished in the construction, repair, or improvement of the homestead (i.e., mechanic's lien claims) and for services performed by laborers or servants.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 514.05, as against the property owner, when does a Minnesota mechanic's lien attach and take effect?
choice_a: Only after the lien statement is recorded with the county recorder
choice_b: From the time the first item of material or labor is furnished upon the premises
choice_c: Only after a court enters judgment in favor of the lien claimant
choice_d: From the date the improvement contract is signed, even if no work has begun
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 514.05, subd. 1 provides that, as against the owner, a mechanic's lien attaches and takes effect from the time the first item of material or labor is furnished on the premises.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 514.05, for a Minnesota mechanic's lien to take priority over a bona fide purchaser, mortgagee, or encumbrancer who has no actual or record notice of the lien, what must have occurred?
choice_a: Mere staking, engineering, land surveying, or soil testing on the site
choice_b: Signing of the construction contract, regardless of any physical work
choice_c: The actual and visible beginning of the improvement on the ground
choice_d: Recording of the building permit application
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 514.05 provides that, as to bona fide purchasers, mortgagees, or encumbrancers without actual or record notice, a mechanic's lien attaches only upon the actual and visible beginning of the improvement on the ground; preliminary activities such as staking, engineering, land surveying, and soil testing do not trigger this attachment.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 514.08, how many days after the last item of work, skill, material, or machinery is furnished does a Minnesota mechanic's lien cease, unless the claimant timely files a lien statement and serves the required notice on the owner?
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: One year
choice_c: 10 days
choice_d: 120 days
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 514.08, subd. 1 provides that a mechanic's lien ceases at the end of 120 days after the last work is done or the last item of skill, material, or machinery is furnished, unless within that period the claimant files a lien statement with the appropriate recording office and serves notice on the owner.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 514.011, a subcontractor or material supplier who wants to preserve mechanic's lien rights on a covered project must generally give the owner written pre-lien notice within how many days after first furnishing labor or materials?
choice_a: 45 days
choice_b: 5 days
choice_c: One year
choice_d: No notice from subcontractors or suppliers is ever required in Minnesota
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 514.011 requires subcontractors and material suppliers to deliver written pre-lien notice to the owner within 45 days after they first furnish labor, skill, or materials, as a prerequisite to preserving full lien rights, subject to certain statutory exceptions.

question: Under Minn. Stat. § 514.011, the general pre-lien notice requirement for improvements to real property does NOT apply to which of the following?
choice_a: A single-family owner-occupied home undergoing a kitchen remodel
choice_b: Improvements to property containing more than four residential units
choice_c: A duplex undergoing a roof replacement
choice_d: A triplex undergoing a foundation repair
explanation: Minn. Stat. § 514.011 exempts improvements to property with more than four residential units, as well as certain larger nonagricultural, nonresidential properties, from the pre-lien notice requirement that otherwise applies to contractors, subcontractors, and material suppliers.
